verdict: Use יְהֹוָה: holam logically on the first he; qamatz on vav.
source_observation: Both inspected crops show conventional Name typography: sheva under yod, qamatz under vav, holam physically above/near the vav head. Other marks above are separate accents. Holam presence was already confirmed.
reason: Physical horizontal placement does not determine the logical base letter. Conventional Name typography can shift the first-he holam above the following consonantal vav even though that vav carries its own qamatz. The dot therefore does not establish two logical vowels on vav. The combined-dot rule concerns a different typographic phenomenon but supports the same separation between logical characters and physical glyph positions.
scope: Correct logical host only. Preserve separately established cantillation, prefixes, and occurrence-specific presence/absence of holam. Do not add marks to other occurrences by analogy.
qualification: The vav-host string is legal Unicode. This verdict concerns appropriate logical transcription, not a claim that Unicode forbids all alternative historical encodings.

evidence.point: Encode logical marks on their proper letters despite merged/shifted physical glyphs.

Primary Unicode proposal documents holam shifted above consonantal vav in the Name even when vav carries another vowel. Used here as typographic evidence, not as a normative mandate for the proposal’s alternative encodings.
